nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 2$, let $s^{[321]}$ be the stack-sorting map whose stack, read from top to bottom, avoids every rotation of $321$ as a consecutive pattern, and let $\mathrm{Sort}_n(s^{[321]})$ be the set of permutations of $[n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$ that $s^{[321]}$ maps to the identity $12 \cdots n$. Then $|\mathrm{Sort}_n(s^{[321]})| = 2^{n-2}$.
nodes.title: Permutations sorted by the consecutive $321$-cyclic stack

nodes.summary: For a sequence $\sigma$, the map $s^{[\sigma]}$ sends a sequence $\pi$ of natural numbers to the output of the following stack procedure. Read $\pi$ from left to right, starting with an empty stack. Before pushing the next entry $x$, pop the fewest entries from the top of the stack, sending them to the output in the order they are removed, so that the stack with $x$ on top, read from top to bottom, contains no…
nodes.title: Consecutive-cyclic-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting map

nodes.summary: Given an optional previous entry $y$ and a sequence $s_1 s_2 \cdots s_\ell$ of natural numbers, this lists, in order, the entries $s_i$ with $s_i \ne s_{i-1} + 1$, where $s_0 = y$; if there is no previous entry, $s_1$ is always listed. With no previous entry, these are the minima $a$ of the maximal blocks $a, a + 1, \dots, a + k$ of adjacent consecutive integers of the sequence.
nodes.title: Heads of runs of consecutive integers

nodes.summary: A sequence $w$ of natural numbers contains a sequence $p = p_1 \cdots p_k$ as a consecutive pattern if some $k$ adjacent entries $w_{i+1}, \dots, w_{i+k}$ of $w$ have the same relative order as $p$: for all $a, b \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, $w_{i+a} < w_{i+b}$ if and only if $p_a < p_b$.
nodes.title: Consecutive pattern containment

nodes.summary: A sequence $w$ of natural numbers contains the pattern $p = p_1 \cdots p_k$ if some subsequence $u_1 \cdots u_k$ of $w$ (whose entries need not be adjacent in $w$) has the same relative order as $p$: for all $a, b \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, $u_a < u_b$ if and only if $p_a < p_b$.
nodes.title: Classical pattern containment in a sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a permutation of $[n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$, written as a sequence, let $\mathrm{red}(\pi)$ be its reduction, of length $\ell$, and let $SC_{[123]}^k$ be the $k$-fold iterate of the cyclic avoidance machine $SC_{[123]}$. For every $k \ge 0$, $SC_{[123]}^k(\pi) = 12 \cdots n$ if and only if $SC_{[123]}^k(\mathrm{red}(\pi)) = 12 \cdots \ell$.
nodes.title: Reduction and iterates of $SC_{(123)}$

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ and let $SC_{[123]}^k$ be the $k$-fold iterate of the cyclic avoidance machine $SC_{[123]}$. For every permutation $\pi$ of $[n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$, $SC_{[123]}^{n-2}(\pi) = 12 \cdots n$, and the bound is tight: $SC_{[123]}^{n-3}(\xi_n) \ne 12 \cdots n$, where $\xi_n$ lists the elements of $[n]$ of parity different from $n$ in increasing order, followed by those of the parity of $n$ in increasing order.
nodes.title: $n - 2$ passes of $SC_{(123)}$ sort every permutation, and $n - 3$ do not

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 4$, let $c = \lceil (2n-1)/3 \rceil$, and let $SC_{[321]}^k$ be the $k$-fold iterate of the cyclic avoidance machine $SC_{[321]}$. For every natural number $m \ge \lceil (n-1-c)/2 \rceil$, $SC_{[321]}^m(12 \cdots n) = SC_{[321]}^{m+c}(12 \cdots n)$.
nodes.title: Eventual periodicity of the identity under $SC_{(321)}$

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 4$ and $1 \le m < \lceil (2n-1)/3 \rceil = \lfloor (2n+1)/3 \rfloor$. Then the cyclic avoidance machine $SC_{[321]}$ maps the superimposition $\mathrm{si}((1, \dots, m), (m+1, \dots, n))$ to $\mathrm{si}((1, \dots, m+1), (m+2, \dots, n))$.
nodes.title: One pass of $SC_{(321)}$ on superimposed increasing runs

nodes.summary: For a sequence $\sigma$, the cyclic avoidance machine $SC_{[\sigma]} = s \circ s_{[\sigma]}$ sends a sequence $\pi$ of natural numbers to $s(s_{[\sigma]}(\pi))$: it first applies the cyclic-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting map $s_{[\sigma]}$, whose stack, read from top to bottom, avoids every rotation of $\sigma$ as a pattern, and then West's stack-sorting map $s$, whose stack, read from top to bottom, avoids the…
nodes.title: Cyclic avoidance machine

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $\sigma$ of natural numbers, the map $s_{[\sigma]}$ sends a finite sequence $\pi$ of natural numbers to the output of the following procedure. Read $\pi$ from left to right, starting with an empty stack. Before pushing the next entry $x$, pop the fewest entries from the top of the stack such that the stack with $x$ pushed on top, read from top to bottom, contains no rotation of $\sigma$ as a…
nodes.title: Cyclic-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting map

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ and let $\mathrm{Sort}_n(s^{[321]})$ be the set of permutations of $[n] = \{1, \ldots, n\}$ that the consecutive-cyclic-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting map $s^{[321]}$ sends to the identity $12 \cdots n$. Every $\pi = \pi_1 \pi_2 \cdots \pi_n$ in $\mathrm{Sort}_n(s^{[321]})$ has $\pi_1 = n$, and $\pi_2 \cdots \pi_n$ is good: each of its entries is the minimum or the maximum of itself and all entries…
nodes.title: First entry and tail of permutations sorted by the consecutive $321$-cyclic stack

nodes.summary: The sequence $51432$ is good (each entry is the minimum or the maximum of itself and all entries after it), and among the six permutations of $\{1, 2, 3\}$ exactly $312$ and $321$ are sent to $123$ by the consecutive-cyclic-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting map $s^{[321]}$.
nodes.title: Small cases of good sequences and of sorting by the consecutive $321$-cyclic stack

nodes.summary: A finite sequence $s = s_1 s_2 \cdots s_\ell$ of natural numbers is good if every entry $s_i$ is the minimum or the maximum of $s_i, s_{i+1}, \ldots, s_\ell$.
nodes.title: Good sequences of suffix extrema

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 2$ and every permutation $\pi$ of $[n] = \{1, \ldots, n\}$, the reduction $\operatorname{red}(\mathrm{SC}_{[123]}(\pi))$ of the image of $\pi$ under the cyclic sorting machine $\mathrm{SC}_{[123]}$ has fewer than $n$ entries.
nodes.title: After one pass of the $123$ cyclic sorting machine, the reduction is shorter

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ and let $\pi = \pi_1 \pi_2 \cdots \pi_n$ be a permutation of $[n] = \{1, \ldots, n\}$. The consecutive-cyclic-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting map $s^{[321]}$ sends $\pi$ to the identity $12 \cdots n$ (that is, $\pi \in \mathrm{Sort}_n(s^{[321]})$) if and only if $\pi_1 = n$ and $\pi_2 \cdots \pi_n$ is good: each of its entries is the minimum or the maximum of itself and all entries after it.
nodes.title: Characterization of the permutations sorted by the consecutive $321$-cyclic stack

nodes.summary: For every permutation $\pi$ of $[n] = \{1, \ldots, n\}$, applying the cyclic sorting machine $\mathrm{SC}_{[123]}$ to the reduction $\operatorname{red}(\pi)$ and reducing the result gives the reduction of $\mathrm{SC}_{[123]}(\pi)$: $\operatorname{red}(\mathrm{SC}_{[123]}(\operatorname{red}(\pi))) = \operatorname{red}(\mathrm{SC}_{[123]}(\pi))$.
nodes.title: Reducing before the $123$ cyclic sorting machine does not change the reduced output

nodes.summary: The reduction $\operatorname{red}(s)$ of a finite sequence $s$ of natural numbers is obtained in two steps. First, every maximal block of adjacent entries of the form $a, a + 1, \ldots, a + k$ is replaced by its first entry $a$. Then the resulting sequence is standardized: each of its entries $x$ is replaced by the number of its entries that are at most $x$, which for distinct entries is the rank of $x$.
nodes.title: Reduction of a sequence

nodes.summary: Fix a property of finite sequences of natural numbers, called bad. Given an input sequence $\pi$ and a stack (listed from top to bottom), read $\pi$ from left to right. Before pushing the next entry $x$, pop the least number $k$ of entries from the top of the stack such that the remaining stack with $x$ pushed on top, read from top to bottom, is not bad (if there is no such $k$, the whole stack is popped and $x$ is…
nodes.title: Restricted stack-sorting from a given stack

nodes.summary: Two finite sequences $s = s_1 \cdots s_\ell$ and $p = p_1 \cdots p_m$ of natural numbers have the same relative order if $\ell = m$ and, for all $1 \le i, j \le m$, $s_i < s_j$ holds if and only if $p_i < p_j$.
nodes.title: Sequences with the same relative order

nodes.summary: Let $s^{[123]}$ be the consecutive-cyclic-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting map for $123$. For every $n \ge 4$, no permutation of $[n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$ is mapped by $s^{[123]}$ to the identity $12 \cdots n$; that is, the set $\mathrm{Sort}_n(s^{[123]})$ of permutations of $[n]$ that $s^{[123]}$ maps to the identity has $0$ elements.
nodes.title: No permutation of length at least four is sorted by the consecutive cyclic $123$-stack

nodes.summary: For a map $f$ from finite sequences of natural numbers to finite sequences of natural numbers and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{Sort}_n(f)$ is the finite set of permutations $\pi$ of $[n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$, written as sequences, such that $f(\pi)$ is the identity permutation $\mathrm{id}_n = 12 \cdots n$.
nodes.title: Permutations sorted by a map

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be West's stack-sorting map, $s_{[123]}$ the cyclic-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting map for $123$, $s^{[123]}$ the consecutive-cyclic-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting map for $123$, and $SC_{[123]} = s \circ s_{[123]}$ the cyclic sorting machine for $123$. Then $s(3124) = 1234$, $s_{[123]}(3124) = 2143$, $s^{[123]}(3124) = 4213$, $SC_{[123]}(3124) = 1234$, $SC_{[123]}(1324) = 3124$ and $SC_{[123]}(231) = 123$.
nodes.title: Stack-sorting examples

nodes.summary: The standardization of $315$ is $\mathrm{st}(315) = 213$, and the reduction of $16783425$ is $\mathrm{red}(16783425) = 15324$. Here $\mathrm{st}$ replaces each entry by its rank, and $\mathrm{red}$ replaces each maximal block of adjacent consecutive integers $a, a + 1, \dots, a + k$ by its minimum $a$ and then standardizes.
nodes.title: Standardization and reduction examples

nodes.summary: The standardization $\mathrm{st}(s)$ of a finite sequence $s = s_1 s_2 \cdots s_k$ of natural numbers is obtained by replacing each entry $s_i$ by the number of indices $j$ with $s_j \le s_i$. When the entries of $s$ are distinct, this number is the rank of $s_i$: the $r$th smallest entry becomes $r$.
nodes.title: Standardization
Superimpose examples

nodes.summary: For finite sequences $a$ and $b$ of natural numbers, $\mathrm{push}(a, b)$ is the sequence obtained by taking the first entry of $b$, then the next two entries of $a$ (only one if just one is left), and repeating; once one of the two sequences is exhausted, the remaining entries of the other follow in order.
nodes.title: Push order of the superimpose operation

nodes.summary: For finite sequences $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$ of natural numbers, let $p = \mathrm{push}(\mathrm{rev}\,\sigma_1, \mathrm{rev}\,\sigma_2)$ be the push order of the superimpose operation on the reversed sequences. Then $\mathrm{si}(\sigma_1, \sigma_2)$ is the reversal of $p$: the stack obtained by pushing the entries of $p$ in order onto an empty stack, read from top to bottom.
nodes.title: Superimpose operation

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $\pi$ of natural numbers, $s(\pi)$ is computed with a stack that starts empty. The entries of $\pi$ are read from left to right; before the next entry $x$ is pushed, the fewest entries are popped from the top of the stack so that the stack with $x$ on top, read from top to bottom, avoids the pattern $21$, and the popped entries are appended to the output in the order in which they are popped.…
nodes.title: West's stack-sorting map

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\xi_n$ list the elements of $[n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$ whose parity differs from that of $n$ in increasing order, followed by the elements with the parity of $n$ in increasing order. Then $\xi_6 = 135246$ and $\xi_7 = 2461357$.
nodes.title: The parity-split permutations for six and seven

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\xi_n$ is the sequence listing the elements of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ whose parity differs from that of $n$ in increasing order, followed by the elements with the same parity as $n$ in increasing order. Thus $\xi_n = 1, 3, \dots, n-1, 2, 4, \dots, n$ for even $n$, and $\xi_n = 2, 4, \dots, n-1, 1, 3, \dots, n$ for odd $n$.
nodes.title: The permutation $\xi_n$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
